prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Three concentric colour zones', subtitle 'Classic target pattern'. One large perfectly FLAT circular paper cut-out seen straight from above on ivory background. Exactly three concentric filled regions: central muted plum/dusky disk, surrounding wide pale cream-pink annulus, outer wide coral-red annulus. No additional rings, pupil, highlight, iris texture or eye shape. Three well-separated navy leader lines end unambiguously inside their own region: 'Dusky centre' ends in central disk; 'Paler middle zone' ends in middle ring; 'Red outer margin' ends in outer coral ring. Small phrase 'Erythema multiforme'. This is paper colour geometry, not actual skin. Bottom text 'Colour model, not a diagnostic skin image'. No body, histology or anatomical cross-section.

teaching.question: What colour arrangement describes a classic erythema multiforme target lesion?
teaching.answer: A dusky centre is surrounded by a paler middle zone and then a red peripheral margin. Clinical assessment is still needed because target-like lesions have multiple causes.

title: Three concentric colour zones
caption: A classic erythema multiforme target has a dusky centre, a paler middle zone and a red outer margin. These flat colour rings illustrate the spatial vocabulary rather than a clinical lesion.
alt: Three concentric painted paper regions—dusky centre, pale middle ring and coral outer ring—are labelled with leaders ending in the correct zone.

review.notes: Exactly three concentric filled regions: dusky plum centre, pale middle annulus, coral-red outer annulus. Each of the three leader dots ends in its correctly named zone. Image is flat paper geometry and states that it is not a diagnostic skin image; no pupil, skin texture or anatomy.
